text.p: Dianon Systems Inc said Tuesday it expects its earnings for the 1996 fiscal year to come in between $0.33 and $0.35 per share.
The lower end of that projection is higher than its most recent forecast in late July, when the company said it expected its 1996 earnings per share to come in between $0.30 and $0.35.
Company President Kevin Johnson also said in a statement that management is "committed to achieving 20 percent to 30 percent annual increases in earnings per share for the next few years."
Chairman Richard Sandberg cautioned that although the company expects continued annual growth in earnings, it does not expect each quarter's earnings per share to exceed the prior quarter's level.

"In the past, the second and fourth quarters of each year have been our strongest quarters," he added. "Based on our historical sales and earnings patterns, shareholders should anticipate that first quarter 1997 earnings per share are likely to be less than fourth quarter 1996 earnings per share and that third quarter 1997 earnings per share may be less than second quarter levels."
In 1995, the company reported a net profit of $0.02 per share after charges from restructuring, severance and investment writedowns.
